candidates.body_md:
## Why choose the FermatMind emotional intelligence test?

Break emotional self-reflection into everyday behaviors you can observe and practice. This 60-item self-report explores Self-Awareness, Emotion Regulation, Empathy and Relationship Management. Results describe your answers in this session and are best considered alongside specific events and feedback.

### Explore four areas of emotional intelligence

Self-Awareness concerns recognizing and describing your feelings; Emotion Regulation concerns responding to them; Empathy concerns understanding others’ situations and possible emotions; Relationship Management concerns expression, listening, collaboration, boundaries and repair. Consider each area separately instead of reducing yourself to “high EQ” or “low EQ.”

Noticing anger does not guarantee you can express a need clearly in that moment. Understanding another person’s feelings does not require sacrificing your boundaries. Real situations help identify which behaviors to practice.

[What does an EQ test measure?](#faq-eq-model)

### How 60 questions become four scores and a 0–100 profile

Responses use a five-point scale from 1 to 5, across Self-Awareness SA, Emotion Regulation ER, Empathy EM and Relationship Management RM, with 15 items each. Positive items use y=x; reverse-keyed items use y=6−x. A response of 2 on a reverse-keyed item contributes 4 points.

Each dimension’s raw sum S=Σy ranges from 15–75; its mean=S÷15; POMP=100×(S−15)÷60. The overall raw sum G ranges from 60–300; overall POMP=100×(G−60)÷240. This rescales the questionnaire range and is not a population percentile. The fields shown in a report depend on its version; not every intermediate quantity in the calculation appears on screen.

[How is the score calculated?](#faq-eq-calculation)

### Standard scores, reference parameters and provisional norms

The scorer first tries to select an applicable reference record. Each dimension uses z=(S−μ)÷σ, where μ is the reference mean and σ the reference standard deviation. Standard score=100+15z, limited to 55–145. The overall score applies the same transformation to the mean of the four dimension z-scores. Estimated percentile=100×Φ(z), using the standard normal cumulative distribution. This is a model conversion, not a direct count of actual participants below your score.

Conditional example: S=60 gives POMP=75. If that report uses μ=53.5 and σ=7.5, z≈0.867 and the standard score is 113. These are example parameters, not verified parameters for every live report. This is not IQ. Read the report’s reference status and version; PROVISIONAL does not establish representative population norms or an ability ranking.

The current report primarily presents an overall standard score and interpretation confidence. The four-dimension matrix shows standard scores, model percentiles and reading bands for SA, ER, EM and RM; the evidence section also identifies reference status. A reading band groups this session’s self-report scores under the version’s rules. It is not an ability qualification or a personality type. Raw sums, means and POMP are scoring quantities; the formula does not establish that each appears on the report screen.

[How should I interpret EQ scores?](#faq-eq-scores)

### Self-report scoring and response-quality checks

This four-dimension self-report aligns positive and reverse-keyed items, aggregates scores and checks response quality. Checks include response speed, repeated identical options, proportions of extreme and midpoint responses, and consistency between paired items. They flag reasons for caution, not diagnoses of EQ or honesty.

This differs from MSCEIT, which assesses reasoning about emotional information through performance tasks. Reverse scoring, standardization and quality checks are measurement procedures; reliability and validity still require evidence for the particular questionnaire and intended use. Another instrument’s research does not validate this one.

[2025 research on ability-based measurement](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychology/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2025.1539785/full)

### Turn results into a communication practice

If naming feelings is difficult, record an event, physical reactions and emotion words. If you react immediately in conflict, try pausing, describing the facts and expressing a need. If misunderstandings recur, paraphrase the other person’s meaning and check your understanding.

Choose one action at a time and record several real interactions. Look for clearer expression and better conflict repair, not merely a higher score at your next test.

[What can I practice after the test?](#faq-eq-growth)

## Frequently asked questions

### What does an EQ test measure? Is emotional intelligence just being sociable?

FermatMind’s EQ-60 explores four self-report dimensions: Self-Awareness, Emotion Regulation, Empathy and Relationship Management. Relationship Management includes expression, listening, collaboration, boundaries and communication repair. Emotional intelligence is not simply Extraversion, always remaining calm or pleasing everyone, and it does not require ignoring your boundaries.

Look at specific behaviors: identifying emotions, understanding triggers, choosing an appropriate expression and listening to feedback. Behavior varies by situation; one “high EQ” or “low EQ” label cannot summarize a person.

### How is a self-report EQ test different from an ability-based emotional intelligence test?

Self-reports ask how you usually understand and handle emotions, so self-awareness and response tendencies influence answers. Ability-based tests assess performance on emotion-related tasks. Their measurement perspectives and scoring differ, and their scores are not equivalent.

FermatMind’s current 60-item form is a self-report, not MSCEIT. Citing emotional intelligence research explains the distinction; it does not imply use, authorization or equivalent validation of that instrument.

[2025 MSCEIT 2 study](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychology/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2025.1539785/full)

### How long does the EQ test take, and how should I answer?

Allow about 10 minutes for 60 items on a 1–5 self-report scale. Each of the four dimensions has 15 items. After item direction is applied, the scorer calculates raw sums, means and POMP scores. Positive items use y=x and reverse-keyed items y=6−x.

Answer according to your usual actual behavior. When a statement feels abstract, recall a recent concrete event rather than answering only for the person you would like to be. Timing, repeated options, response proportions and paired-item consistency inform response-quality flags. They do not add EQ points or establish psychometric reliability or validity.

Before answering, read the Privacy Policy. It explains that the service may process assessment responses, generated reports and device or log data, and describes uses and privacy requests. Access, correction or deletion requests can be made through support; some records may need to be retained. Free testing does not itself establish anonymity or immediate deletion.

[Read the Privacy Policy](/en/privacy)

[Start the EQ-60 test](#choose-version)

### Is this emotional intelligence test scientifically valid?

Emotional intelligence has different theories and measurement methods. Sharing the name EQ does not make instruments equivalent. Evaluate evidence for FermatMind’s specific questionnaire, language, population and intended use, rather than borrowing another scale’s conclusions.

EQ-60 currently labels content evidence preliminary and references provisional. Internal consistency, retest stability, the four-dimension structure, external associations and language/group invariance remain planned validation work. The report can organize this session’s self-descriptions; it should not be presented as an ability measure with completed comprehensive reliability and validity evidence. Recognizing yourself in a description is not scientific validation.

For example, if you describe yourself as calm when criticized, examine what you actually said in a recent disagreement and whether you understood the concern. A mismatch deserves investigation of the situation; it does not establish dishonesty.

[Reliability and validity](/en/reliability-validity)

### How should I interpret EQ scores? Are they comparable to IQ?

The scorer first tries to select an applicable reference record. Each dimension uses z=(S−μ)÷σ. Standard score=100+15z, limited to 55–145. The overall score transforms the mean of the four dimension z-scores. Estimated percentile=100×Φ(z), a standard normal model conversion rather than a direct empirical population rank.

Conditional example: S=60 gives POMP 75; if μ=53.5 and σ=7.5 are used, the standard score is 113. Do not assume every live report uses these parameters. 113 is not IQ, POMP 75 is not the 75th percentile, and PROVISIONAL does not establish a representative reference sample. Comparisons need the same instrument, version, language and applicable reference; language/group equivalence still needs testing.

### Can emotional intelligence improve? What can I practice after the test?

Emotional behaviors can be practice goals, but taking a test does not guarantee improvement, and a short-term score increase does not establish effectiveness. Choose a concrete observable behavior instead of an abstract goal of “higher EQ.”

After a disagreement, record the trigger, feelings, action and feedback. Next time, try clarifying the other person’s meaning before expressing your needs. Compare changes in real interactions over time and seek appropriate support when useful.

### Is the EQ test free? Does a low score mean I need to buy help?

FermatMind’s current 60-item EQ test and results are free. Your score does not determine eligibility to see the currently provided results or mean you must buy a service to improve.

Understand the score and your circumstances before choosing learning or support resources. Free testing here does not make other courses, consultations or professional assessments free. Do not base a spending or health decision solely on one online score.

### Does low EQ indicate a mental health condition or poor leadership potential?

No. An EQ self-report is not a clinical diagnosis and cannot independently determine leadership ability, relationship quality or morality. Roles, stress, skills and environment also influence behavior.

Use results to identify situations where support may help, avoiding labels for yourself or others. Persistent emotional distress affecting life warrants qualified assessment; an EQ score cannot replace a diagnosis.

Do not use EQ-60 for hiring, promotion, role assignment or performance appraisal. Adding other information does not make this self-report appropriate as a screening basis for those decisions.

[Assessment methods and limitations](/en/method-boundaries)

### How can I tell whether a change in my EQ score reflects progress?

First check that version, conditions and response standards are comparable. Changed self-awareness, recent events, impression management or remembering items can affect scores; one change does not establish growth or decline.

Combine scores with behavior records: are your choices different under similar stress or conflict, and is communication feedback consistently improving? Avoid repeated testing for a preferred score or treating small fluctuations as firm conclusions.

### How is the emotional intelligence score calculated?

Responses use a five-point scale from 1 to 5, across SA, ER, EM and RM, with 15 items each. Positive items use y=x; reverse-keyed items use y=6−x. A response of 2 on a reverse-keyed item contributes 4 points.

Each dimension’s raw sum S=Σy ranges from 15–75; mean=S÷15; POMP=100×(S−15)÷60. Overall raw sum G ranges from 60–300; overall POMP=100×(G−60)÷240. A dimension raw sum of 60 gives a mean of 4 and POMP 75. This is not a population percentile.

### Do open EQ scoring formulas establish scientific validity?

This four-dimension self-report aligns positive and reverse-keyed items, aggregates scores and checks response quality. Checks include response speed, repeated identical options, proportions of extreme and midpoint responses, and consistency between paired items. They flag reasons for caution, not diagnoses of EQ or honesty.

This differs from MSCEIT’s performance tasks. Reverse scoring, standardization and quality checks are measurement procedures. Reliability and validity require evidence for the instrument and its intended use. Another instrument’s research does not validate this one.

[2025 research on ability-based measurement](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychology/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2025.1539785/full)
